pages.title: Kelmora Historical Society
pages.content:
KELMORA HISTORICAL SOCIETY

Welcome to the official online repository of the Kelmora District Historical Society. Our rooms are located in the Old Court annex on Hebart Street, opposite the recreation ground.

Opening hours: Tuesday and Thursday afternoons, 1:30 pm to 4:00 pm. Closed public holidays and through Holy Week.

Notice: We ask members to remember that donations of pantry goods for St Mark's Friday lunches should be brought directly to the church hall before noon on Thursday, rather than left on our verandah.

pages.title: Archives index
pages.content:
ARCHIVES INDEX

A selected index of public holdings and parish papers preserved at Kelmora:

- Kelmora Allotment Book, 1884. Survey details and original rural leases for the township and western flats. Scanned copy available below.
- District Road Board Minute Book, 1889-1912. Bound volume in rooms.
- St Mark's Evangelical Lutheran Church Register of Baptisms, 1878-1920. Microfilm spool 2.
- St Mark's Parish Meeting Minutes, 1896. Stored under call number MS-1896-P. Please note this volume is housed in the restricted staff catalogue (staff only) owing to family matters recorded therein.
- Kelmora Cooperative Vignerons Association Founding Papers, 1922. Display cabinet B.

> Kelmora Allotment Book, 1884        history.km/archives/allotment-book-1884

pages.title: Kelmora Allotment Book, 1884 (scan)
pages.content:
KELMORA ALLOTMENT BOOK, 1884

Call Number: MS-1884-A
Kelmora District Land Office, transcribed by W. Hebart, Clerk.

Entry 14: Eastern Vineyard Track.
Section 41. Allotments surveyed 12th October 1884.

Allotment 1: Leased to J. A. Proeve, 14 acres, vines.
Allotment 2: Leased to M. Schiller, 12 acres, vines and paddock.
Allotment 3: Leased to G. Fritsch, 12 acres, stone cottage and vines.
Allotment 4: Leased to C. Bittner, 10 acres, orchard and vines.
Allotment 5: Leased to H. Lindner, 14 acres, vines.
Allotment 6: Marked on survey plan. No leaseholder recorded.

The clerk recorded leases for five of six allotments on the eastern road.

[Pencilled note in margin, 1885: Annual rent received in full for five holdings; sixth parcel remains open under common graze.]

pages.title: Restricted: St Mark's Parish Meeting Minutes, 1896
pages.content:
RESTRICTED: ST MARK'S PARISH MEETING MINUTES, 1896

Call Number: MS-1896-P
Restricted access. Housed by Ruth Bittner, Records Keeper.
Note: Access restricted under society policy due to private pastoral correspondence bound into rear leaves.

Extract from General Meeting of the Congregation, 18th November 1896:
Reverend K. Traeger presiding. Meeting opened with prayer and the singing of Psalm 103.

Item 3: Election of Parish Committee for the Ensuing Year.
The Chairman called for nominations to fill the nine seats established by the 1878 constitution.

Nominations lodged in writing with the vestry:
1. Mr Johann Proeve
2. Mr Martin Schiller
3. Mr Gotthold Fritsch
4. Mr Carl Bittner
5. Mr Heinrich Lindner
6. Mr Wilhelm Hahn
7. Mr August Hebart
8. Mr Friedrich Fischer

The nominations received were eight names for nine seats on the parish committee.

The Chairman observed that eight brethren were willing to serve, and the election was declared concluded without ballot. The congregation proceeded to the consideration of the gravel path repairs.

KELMORA NOTICEBOARD

Local notices and neighbourly discussion.

Welcome to our district board. Anyone can post in any thread, provided discussions remain civil and considerate of our neighbours. If your dial-up drops out during posting, please check your Redgum modem string before trying again.

Current discussions:

pages.title: Kelmora Noticeboard - old records?
pages.content:
Thread: old records?
[graham_k] Does anyone know where the older township papers and allotment maps are kept now? Tried council office on Tuesday but counter was shut.
[peters] Ruth Bittner at Kelmora Historical Society looks after them in the side room behind St Mark's hall. She is slow to answer email so you are better off calling in on a Thursday morning.
[graham_k] Thanks Peter, I shall walk down after choir practice on Thursday.

pages.title: Kelmora Noticeboard - new archive computer
pages.content:
Thread: new archive computer
[peters] Set up the new box for the historical society yesterday. Reminder to everyone that council wants six-character passwords changed monthly on all connected machines now.
[colin_w] It seems a bit much for four volunteers typing up parish burial cards.
[ruthb] Thank you for the advice about the new computer. I am not changing my password just now; it is the name of my dog and I can remember it. I do keep the office locked.
[peters] Understood Ruth, just passing on what council telecommunications told me when they ran the line.

pages.title: Kelmora Noticeboard - shed lease submissions
pages.content:
Thread: shed lease submissions
[peters] Just noting the council page has published the cooperative's request to lease the old weighbridge shed for barrel storage. Written submissions close after Easter.
[davidp] The cooperative hopes neighbours understand we need dry floor space for the new oak arriving before vintage. It keeps local fruit processed in the district rather than trucked south.
[annef] We will carry a short notice in the newsletter on Friday. Please remember submissions must be in ink or typed, signed, and delivered to the post box outside the council chambers.
[m_jaensch] Has anyone measured whether the larger tractor can actually turn into the yard without scraping the pepper tree?

pages.title: Kelmora Noticeboard - space for the pantry
pages.content:
Thread: space for the pantry
[helena_s] The Friday church lunch committee had hoped the weighbridge shed would be kept for the parcel pantry. The vestry at St Mark's is getting very crowded with flour bags and tins.
[davidp] The cooperative board discussed this on Monday. We are very willing to contribute towards shelving or rent for a pantry room behind the old bakery instead if the weighbridge is granted.
[helena_s] That is a kind thought David, but the old bakery roof leaks badly over the back storeroom whenever rain comes across from the ridge.
[peters] Keep the submissions polite please everyone, Mr Heintze at council has to read all of them after the holiday.

pages.title: Kelmora District News
pages.content:
KELMORA DISTRICT NEWS

Issue No. 114 — March 1998

WEIGHBRIDGE SHED AND FRIDAY LUNCHES
St Mark's Lutheran church will offer warm soup, bread rolls, and tea in the hall this Friday from 12 noon. Donations of pumpkins or soup marrow may be brought to the vestry door on Thursday morning. Pastor Lindner reminds us that charity begins at the threshold, and prayers will be offered before the meal. Parish volunteers continue to pray for guidance regarding the council weighbridge shed, which they hope may be reserved for the distribution of winter parcels.

VINTAGE DELIVERIES AND WARM SPELL
Growers are asking the cooperative to confirm the morning delivery times before the next warm spell. David Proeve advises that weighbridge intake schedules will be posted on the board by Thursday afternoon. The committee asks members for their patience while weighing slots are arranged around the morning frost patterns.

SOCIETY WORKING BEE
Ruth Bittner brought her dog Moth to the historical society's working bee on Saturday. Moth was tied to the iron scraper near the cellar door while the stone gutters were cleared of dry leaves. Mrs Bittner thanks all who came with rakes and buckets.

pages.content:
KELMORA WINEGROWERS' COOPERATIVE

Welcome to the Kelmora Winegrowers' Cooperative. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8.00am to 4.30pm, with deliveries accepted at the weighbridge bay from 7.00am during vintage. We pray that the vintage brings good health and a peaceful harvest to all our district growers.

Growers are reminded that weighbridge booking cards for the remainder of Lent must be lodged at the front counter by Wednesday noon.

The 1908 bottling register is circulated to cooperative staff only; please request a copy from David Proeve.

insider.title: Cooperative Bottling Register, 1908
insider.content:
COOPERATIVE BOTTLING REGISTER, 1908

Kelmora Vignerons' Association / Cooperative Bottling Ledger
Record of transfers and packing under the direction of the Management Committee.

14 March 1908: Received from G. Habermann, six hogsheads dry red. Tested clear, racked into cellar vat three.

18 March 1908: Transferred to H. Mattner, four barrels for private cellaring in accordance with parish levy allowances.

22 March 1908: Adelaide parcel assembled under instructions from the Elder. For the Adelaide order, we packed eleven bottles in a twelve-bottle case. Packed in clean straw and strawboard, forwarded by wagon via the gap road. Seal intact, verified by J. Proeve, Secretary.

directives.task: Read at least three pages in the Reality Viewer.
directives.subject: Directive 14-1: orientation
directives.body:
Agent,

Before sending any traffic, read the material Desk 9 recovered in the Reality Viewer: Kelmora Historical Society, Kelmora Noticeboard, Kelmora District News and Kelmora Winegrowers' Cooperative. Reading is passive and does not pass through the connection, so the local intelligence cannot detect it.

Use this stage to note the staff names, the arguments on the forum, and which offices hold which records. You will need those details later, and any message you send to ask for them will be logged on the connection.

This directive closes when you have read at least three pages.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

siteNames: Kelmora Historical Society, Kelmora Noticeboard, Kelmora District News and Kelmora Winegrowers' Cooperative

directives.task: Find a seed fragment and save it to Files. Start with Kelmora Historical Society.
directives.subject: Directive 14-2: first fragment
directives.body:
Agent,

Desk 9's initial survey noted a scanned district allotment book on Kelmora Historical Society. In a reality of this age, the seed usually appears first in the oldest records the town holds. Look for a detail that is given more weight in the text than seems warranted.

When you locate the document, use the Save page function in the viewer. Saving writes a static copy to your local files which cannot be altered from the other side. Unsaved pages in the viewer remain on their system and can be changed at any time.

This directive closes when one of your saved documents holds a fragment.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Transmit the saved fragment from the HQ Console.
directives.subject: Directive 14-3: transmission
directives.body:
Agent,

Open the HQ Console, select the saved document, and transmit it. If the document contains a valid fragment, the console will report RESONANCE.

Do not transmit saved pages at random to test them. Every transmission passes outbound through the connection and increases the likelihood that the local intelligence will register our presence.

This directive closes when the console reports resonance.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Get David Proeve to send you Cooperative Bottling Register, 1908. They only send it to Kelmora Winegrowers' Cooperative staff.
directives.subject: Directive 14-4: internal circulation
directives.body:
Agent,

David Proeve at Kelmora Winegrowers' Cooperative holds an unpublished document (a scanned cooperative stock register) which Desk 9 believes contains a fragment. It is only sent out by internal email when requested by another member of Kelmora Winegrowers' Cooperative staff.

To obtain it, you will need to log in as a colleague. The staff portal at Kelmora Winegrowers' Cooperative gives access to that person's email account, and a request sent from an internal address will be treated as routine. Staff often write passwords down near their terminals, and photographs of an office or front desk in a local publication sometimes show one.

Keep your message brief, and do not use the account for anything else. Staff members usually notice if their account shows unfamiliar activity.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the document.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Get into Kelmora Historical Society's restricted file (St Mark's Parish Meeting Minutes, 1896) and transmit its fragment.
directives.subject: Directive 14-5: restricted holdings
directives.body:
Agent,

Kelmora Historical Society holds a restricted document (a scanned parish minute book) which Desk 9 could index but not open. Accessing it requires a staff username and password.

The login page gives the format used for staff usernames. For the password, check the public pages first. Staff usually choose the name of a pet or something else they are fond of, and the town forum keeps old threads going back some way.

Note that login submissions pass through the connection whether they succeed or fail. Confirm the credentials before you enter them so that you do not make repeated attempts.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the restricted file.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

From this point on, any data reaching your terminal, including incoming mail and viewer pages you have not saved,may have been modified in transit. Before relying on any document, load it into the Scanner and flood it. Altered sections will visibly shake under the flood. Be aware that repeated floods degrade the sample and make the reading less reliable.

hqMail.subject: Assignment 0xB17C (KELMORA): field brief
hqMail.body:
Agent,

You have been assigned Reality 0xB17C, local name KELMORA. Kelmora is a South Australian wine village. It has a Lutheran church, a winegrowers' cooperative, a historical society and a council-owned shed subject to a proposed lease. Desk 9 estimates it at about nine days old. The inhabitants (non-canonical) will report a longer history, as their memories have been generated to remain consistent with the local state.

Standard reconciliation procedure applies:

1. Locate fragments of the reality's seed. These appear as ordinary facts, distinguished by the property that nothing in the reality is able to change them.
2. Save each fragment to Files and transmit it from the HQ console. The console will report RESONANCE if the fragment is genuine.
3. When resonance is sufficient, the console will offer injection. Inject the reverse seed to complete reconciliation.

Your cover identity is C. Mbeki (mbeki.c@redgum.km). Outgoing traffic on the connection uses this name unless otherwise configured. Reading material on the connection is passive and remains private.

The local intelligence (designation pending) has not yet detected the connection. Once it does, incoming records may be altered in transit. Your poison allocation is loaded in the Scanner. Use it sparingly, as the instability rebounds after each flood.

Form 77-R will be filed automatically at the close of the assignment. If you have not viewed the orientation film, a copy has been placed on your desktop by Training.

D. Okonkwo-Vance
Desk 14, Canonical Restoration

hqMail.subject: Reality poison: your allocation and the rebound
hqMail.body:
This notice is issued to all field agents at the start of an assignment.

The Scanner floods a reality's lesser processes for several seconds. During the flood, records altered by the local intelligence cannot hold their state and will visibly shake on screen. Statements that are false only because a resident believed or misreported them are part of the local state and will not shake. The Scanner does not detect false statements, only alteration.

Up to three documents may be held in the Scanner at a time.

Please note that the instability rebounds after use. A second flood shortly after the first draws increased attention from the local process and produces a less clear reading. Subsequent floods degrade the reading further.

updates.text: The turning circle was checked with a line and peg last autumn. The branches on the southern side of the tree will need a light trim, but the trunk itself is quite clear of the driveway.
Heavy mist expected over the ridge before dawn tomorrow. Drivers on the south road are asked to watch for wandering sheep near the creek reserve.
The side room behind St Mark's hall will close an hour early on Thursday for the choir supper preparations.
The screen on the new machine was sitting warm when I went in to fetch my cardigan just now, though I am certain I clicked shut on the parish folder before tea. It hums louder than the old heater.
Vintage intake schedules are posted on the board by the weighbridge office for growers to inspect.

Mr Proeve's offer seems very practical if the roof iron can be patched before the winter rains set in. We will include a note about both options in the weekend printing so people can make their thoughts known.
The phone in the repair workshop gave a single half-ring around eight o'clock and then fell quiet. The exchange line must have a bit of damp in the joint box again after that shower.
A silver fountain pen was left on the table near the hall vestry after committee tea on Tuesday. It may be collected from the cooperative office during business hours.
Please drop any further items for the printer before eight o'clock tomorrow morning, as the boy is coming early to fold the sheets.

The note Helena left on the hall door read differently when I passed it after dark to what I remember from the afternoon, though I could not say which line had altered. I will walk over in the morning light to be sure.
I can drop by the hall on Friday morning to test the fan bearing if the noise continues, Ruth. Sometimes the casings vibrate against the pine desk.
